python-fundamentals.q: Which Python function displays an order number on screen?
python-fundamentals.why: A call to print sends a readable representation to the output.
Python evaluates the addition before displaying the result.

python-fundamentals.q: What does the # symbol begin outside a quoted string?
python-fundamentals.why: Python skips the rest of that line when executing the program.

variables.q: Which is text in Python, "007" or 7?
variables.why: Quotes preserve the three typed characters, including the leading zeros.

variables.q: After count = 3 and count = count + 1, what value does count hold?
variables.why: The right-hand side uses the previous value before the new assignment.

variables.q: What built-in function reports the type of a stored value?
variables.why: type(value) tells you whether the current value is an integer, string or another kind of object.

strings.q: What index identifies the first letter of a Python string?
strings.why: The first position is offset zero from the beginning.

strings.q: What is the length of the string "A B", including its space?
strings.why: A space is a character, just as A and B are.
The slice keeps positions 1, 2 and 3 and stops before 4.

numbers.q: How many full boxes of six can be filled with 17 eggs?
numbers.why: Two boxes hold 12 eggs and the remaining five cannot fill another box.

numbers.q: Which Python operator finds the remainder after division?
numbers.why: For 17 eggs and boxes of six, 17 % 6 equals 5.
Two asterisks denote exponentiation, so 3 is multiplied by itself.

conditions.q: Which keyword introduces the first test in a Python decision?
conditions.why: The block under if runs when its test succeeds.

conditions.q: What comparison symbol includes equality in “at least 12”?
In one if/elif/else chain, how many branches can run at most?
conditions.why: Python stops at the first matching branch.

predicates.q: In plain English, what two answers can a predicate give?
predicates.why: A predicate decides whether one item has the property being tested.

predicates.q: Does 5 < 5 evaluate to True or False?
A request meets one of two requirements. Which word joins them if either one is sufficient?
predicates.why: The combined predicate succeeds when at least one requirement succeeds.

loops.q: How many times does a loop visit the items in [4, 4, 0]?
loops.why: A loop visits each position, including repeated or zero values.

loops.q: Which statement skips the rest of the current iteration?
loops.why: continue moves to the next item without ending the loop.

loops.q: Which statement leaves the nearest loop immediately?
loops.why: No later items in that loop are visited.

lists.q: What is the index of the second shopping-list item?
lists.why: Python list indexing starts at zero.

lists.q: Which list method adds one item at the end?
lists.why: append keeps the existing order and places the new item after the last one.
An empty list has no positions to count.

tuples.q: How many values does the coordinate (2, 7) contain?
tuples.why: The comma separates aisle and shelf into two positions.

tuples.q: Which punctuation mark makes (5,) a one-item tuple?
tuples.why: Parentheses alone can simply group an expression.

tuples.q: Can a tuple's first slot be reassigned after creation? Answer yes or no.
tuples.why: A tuple fixes the sequence of object references it contains.

sets.q: How many distinct names are in the set made from Jo, Jo and Mo?
sets.why: Repeated equal entries occupy one membership position.

sets.q: Which set operation keeps names appearing in both groups?
sets.why: A name must belong to both sets to appear in their intersection.

sets.q: Which Python call creates an empty set?
sets.why: Empty braces create a dictionary. Calling set with no items creates a set.

dictionaries.q: In {"Jo": "204"}, which text is the key?
dictionaries.why: A key is the identifier used to look up the associated value.

dictionaries.q: If the same key is assigned a new value, how many entries for that key remain?
dictionaries.why: A dictionary maps a key to one current value.

dictionaries.q: Which dictionary method accepts a fallback for an absent key?
dictionaries.why: contacts.get(name, fallback) returns the fallback when the key is absent.

functions.q: Which keyword sends a result back to a function's caller?
functions.why: Returning a value makes it available for the next calculation.

functions.q: What value comes back when a Python function ends without a return value?
functions.why: Displaying a total with print alone leaves the caller with None.

functions.q: What is the name for an input variable listed in a function definition?
functions.why: An argument supplies a value to that parameter when the function is called.

recursion.q: What is the usual name for a case that finishes without another recursive call?
recursion.why: A base case lets the chain of calls unwind.

recursion.q: How many files should a recursive count return for an empty folder?
recursion.why: There are no file contributions to add.

recursion.q: In count([a, [b, c]]), how many files does the inner folder contribute?
recursion.why: The nested call counts b and c before handing that total to its parent.

comprehensions.q: What kind of collection does [x for x in items] produce?
comprehensions.why: Square brackets collect the results into a new list.

comprehensions.q: In [x * 2 for x in [2, 3]], what is the second output value?
comprehensions.why: The mapping expression doubles the second input, 3.

comprehensions.q: Does the if clause in a list comprehension filter or sort the input?
comprehensions.why: The condition determines whether each input contributes an output.

file-handling.q: Which file mode adds entries at the end without truncating a log?
file-handling.why: Append mode preserves earlier entries and places writes at the end.

file-handling.q: Which Python keyword opens a context that closes a file when the block exits?
file-handling.why: The context manager closes the file even if the block raises an error.

file-handling.q: What character sequence represents a line break in a Python string literal?
file-handling.why: The newline separates one text line from the next.

exceptions.q: Which exception does int("milk") normally raise?
exceptions.why: The value is text but its contents cannot be parsed as an integer.

exceptions.q: Which keyword introduces the handler for a matching Python exception?
exceptions.why: Python transfers control to a matching except block.

exceptions.q: Which clause runs as a try statement finishes, including during an exception?
exceptions.why: Cleanup such as releasing a resource belongs in a finally block.

oop.q: What do we call one particular book created from a Book class?
oop.why: The class describes shared structure. An instance has its own identity and state.

oop.q: Which conventional parameter names the current Python instance in an instance method?
oop.why: self lets a method read or update this particular book.

oop.q: Two books each track their own borrowed flag. Is that instance state or class state?
oop.why: Changing one copy's status should leave the other copy's flag alone.

modules.q: Which keyword makes a Python module available by name in a program?
modules.why: After import math, the name math refers to the loaded module.

modules.q: After import math, what expression calls the integer square-root function on 9?
modules.why: The dot selects the function from the module's namespace.

modules.q: What file extension does an ordinary Python source module use?
modules.why: A file such as fees.py can contain related functions and constants.

virtual-environments.q: What is the standard-library module used by python -m venv?
virtual-environments.why: It creates a project directory containing a separate interpreter environment.

virtual-environments.q: Which command suffix identifies pip for the Python interpreter you explicitly invoked: -m pip or -m git?
virtual-environments.why: Running python -m pip installs through the selected interpreter.

virtual-environments.q: Does activating an environment automatically install a project's missing libraries? Answer yes or no.
virtual-environments.why: Activation changes command lookup. Installing packages is a separate operation.

git.q: Which Git command stages a changed file for the next commit?
git.why: Staging selects the content that the next normal commit records.

git.q: Which Git command shows staged, modified and untracked files?
git.why: Status summarizes the working tree and staging area.

git.q: Does a local commit automatically upload itself to a remote repository? Answer yes or no.
git.why: A push is a separate operation that transfers commits.

dsa.q: Which structure serves the most recently added item first?
dsa.why: Last in, first out matches the way an inner opening bracket must close first.

dsa.q: Which structure normally serves the earliest waiting customer first?
dsa.why: First in, first out preserves arrival order.

dsa.q: How many unmatched openings remain after reading the text "(()"?
dsa.why: Two brackets open and the final bracket closes the most recent one.

complexity.q: Scanning 8 items once needs how many item visits?
complexity.why: The visit count grows in direct proportion to the input length.

complexity.q: What is the usual Big-O label for a fixed number of operations independent of n?
complexity.why: The operation count stays bounded as the input grows.

complexity.q: If an algorithm stores a second copy of n items, what is the extra-space order?
complexity.why: The number of additional stored items grows with n.

database-fundamentals.q: In a registration table, what normally represents one registration: a row or a column?
database-fundamentals.why: Columns describe fields. A row groups field values for one record.

database-fundamentals.q: What name is given to the identifier that uniquely identifies a row?
database-fundamentals.why: A stable primary key lets other records refer to a specific row.

database-fundamentals.q: What does SQL use to represent a missing value?
database-fundamentals.why: NULL indicates the field has no known value.

sql.q: Which clause chooses the columns to return?
sql.why: The list following SELECT defines the output columns or expressions.

sql.q: Which clause filters individual rows before they enter the result?
sql.why: Rows enter the result only when their filter condition is true.

sql.q: Which clause specifies the order of the returned rows?
sql.why: A query needs an explicit ordering when a predictable sequence matters.

database-engines.q: Which engine commonly stores an entire local database in a single main file: SQLite or PostgreSQL?
database-engines.why: SQLite runs in the application process and reads its database file.

database-engines.q: Which term describes SQL work saved successfully at the end of a transaction?
database-engines.why: A commit makes the transaction's results part of the database.

database-engines.q: What database name does Python's sqlite3 use for a connection-local in-memory database?
database-engines.why: That database normally disappears when the connection closes.

tables.q: Which constraint requires a nonmissing value?
tables.why: The database rejects writes that omit the required value.
A check expression can rule out a negative balance.

tables.q: What SQL statement defines a new table?
tables.why: The statement declares column names, types and constraints.

crud.q: Which SQL command adds a new employee row?
Which command changes fields on existing rows?
crud.why: UPDATE modifies the rows selected by its condition.

crud.q: Which command removes matching rows while keeping the table definition?
crud.why: DELETE removes data rows from the table.

joins.q: Which join retains every left-hand row even without a matching right-hand row?
joins.why: Right-side fields become NULL where no match exists.

joins.q: A cross join combines 2 employees with 3 departments. How many pairs result?
joins.why: Every employee pairs with every department.

joins.q: When an employee has two matching rows on the other side of an inner join, how many result rows does that employee contribute?
joins.why: A join emits a row for each matching pair.

subqueries.q: What is the term for a query nested inside another query?
subqueries.why: The outer query can use the inner rows or value.

subqueries.q: What is AVG of the nonmissing salaries 10, 20 and 30?
subqueries.why: Their total is 60 and there are three salaries.

subqueries.q: Which SQL keyword tests whether a subquery returns at least one row?
subqueries.why: The test cares about the presence of a row.

aggregation.q: Which aggregate counts all rows, even those with missing fields?
aggregation.why: The star counts rows independently of any one field.

aggregation.q: Which clause forms one group per team?
aggregation.why: Rows sharing the grouping key are summarized together.

aggregation.q: Which clause filters completed groups after aggregation?
aggregation.why: HAVING can test a group total such as SUM(amount).

indexes.q: A database index can speed up lookups but takes extra disk space. Does it also need maintenance during writes? Answer yes or no.
indexes.why: Inserted, deleted or changed indexed entries have to be reflected in the index.

indexes.q: In an index on (team, date), what is the leftmost key?
indexes.why: The leading component determines the initial grouping of entries.

indexes.q: What SQLite command prefix shows how a query will be executed?
indexes.why: The plan can show whether a scan or an index lookup is chosen.

transactions.q: Which command makes all successful work in a SQL transaction permanent?
transactions.why: A commit ends the transaction with its changes saved.
Rolling back restores the state from before the transaction.

transactions.q: Which property means both account updates happen together or neither takes effect?
transactions.why: Atomicity treats multiple changes as a single unit.

database-design.q: Which key points from an employee record to its department record?
database-design.why: The reference expresses a relationship between two tables.

database-design.q: If three employees share one department row, how many copies of the department phone should be stored in that design?
database-design.why: The phone belongs to the department and can be looked up through the shared reference.

database-design.q: What is the relationship called when one department has many employees?
database-design.why: Several rows on the employee side can refer to one department.
